title: Empirical evaluation of generate–verify–repair (GVR) for LLM-generated network configurations — repaired preregistration
research_question: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline materially reduce verifier-detected semantic-failure rates of LLM-generated device-level network configurations compared to an LLM-only pipeline under a matched per-task model-call budget?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: An LLM-only pipeline will produce a nonzero verifier-detected semantic-failure rate on intent-to-configuration tasks.

H2 (primary): A GVR pipeline that iteratively invokes the LLM with deterministic verifier feedback (up to 3 repairs; 4 LLM calls max per pipeline attempt) will produce a higher verifier-pass rate than an LLM-only pipeline under a matched maximum model-call budget, tested on a paired task set using the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline estimand.
H3: The absolute and relative reduction in semantic-failure rate from GVR will vary by task complexity (larger gains on low/medium complexity; diminishing returns on highest complexity).
exploratory_questions: Does the GVR effect replicate qualitatively on a second hosted LLM API (exploratory, not primary confirmatory analysis)?
How many repair iterations are actually used when GVR succeeds (distribution of iterations), and what is model-call cost per successful pass?
benchmark_scope: Public and synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks curated from public NetOps benchmarks and synthetic generators (see Sampling Plan provenance).
Verifiable properties limited to those expressible in the chosen deterministic verifier (reachability, ACL semantics, simple routing-invariant checks as documented below).
model_scope: Primary (confirmatory): OpenAI/gpt-4o-mini (hosted API) — generation settings: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.0, max_tokens=1500, deterministic-seed-protocol: fixed prompt + fixed per-attempt seed token where API supports explicit seeds; where explicit seeds unavailable, deterministic settings (temperature=0, top_p=0) are used and outputs archived.
Exploratory: Anthropic/claude-2.1 (hosted API) — generation settings: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.0, max_tokens=1500; used for exploratory replication only.
transformation_scope: Config canonicalization: whitespace normalization, deterministic ordering of multi-line statements where semantically neutral, canonical interface and ACL name mapping.
Parsing into verifier input format (Batfish snapshot/harness) with deterministic, idempotent transformation rules.
No human annotation; all mapping/normalization rules implemented as deterministic code pipelines with unit tests.
secondary_estimands: Per-complexity paired success-rate differences (low / medium / high complexity strata)
Counts of tasks converted from fail→pass by GVR (per-task indicator)
Distribution of repair iterations for successful GVR cases
Model-call cost per successful verified pass (mean, median)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: 132 paired tasks stratified equally by declared complexity into three strata (low=44, medium=44, high=44). Derivation: power calculation (see Power Plan) requires n=132 paired episodes to detect an absolute paired pass-rate difference of 0.15 with two-sided alpha=0.05 and 80% power under conservative variance assumptions; we therefore set confirmatory N=132. Tasks will be sourced deterministically from (1) public NetOps benchmark artifacts referenced in evidence (NetConfEval-like public datasets where licensing permits) and (2) synthetic generator scripts included in the artifact. Provenance rules: (a) select all publicly redistributable tasks matching the target domain (ACLs, reachability, routing invariants, mixed policies); (b) if public pool <132, generate synthetic tasks via seeded generator seeded with fixed RNG seed S_confirm=20260801 to reach 132; (c) label complexity by deterministic rule-based rubric (complexity score = ACL rule count + distinct-device-count + number-of-invariants; thresholds pre-registered: low<=5, medium 6-12, high>12); (d) held-out ordering: tasks shuffled with fixed RNG seed and split into confirmatory (first 132) and exploratory (next 40) sets; (e) store full task JSONs and content-addressable hashes in the artifact bundle. Each task yields one paired episode (LLM-only vs GVR) for the primary model.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 implementing the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline estimand. Primary test: paired binary comparison using McNemar-style exact test (or paired permutation test if assumptions unmet) to test difference in verifier-pass indicators between GVR and LLM-only across the 132 paired tasks (primary model only). Bootstrap (10000 replicates) 95% CI for paired pass-rate difference. Sensitivity analyses: (1) treat failed/timeout API calls per 'failed_call_treatment' (primary: 'complete_pair_primary' meaning pairs with unrecoverable API/infrastructure failures will be excluded from primary analysis and reported in a failure table; (2) robustness sensitivity: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' — treat failed pipeline calls as failures (worst-case) and recompute). Exploratory analyses: per-complexity strata effects, per-model replication (exploratory model), repair-iteration distribution, model-call cost per successful pass. All code and raw outputs archived to enable re-execution; analysis seeds for bootstrap set to 20260802.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory claim is the single estimand above. No alpha correction for the primary test. Stratum (complexity) and exploratory-model analyses are explicitly exploratory and will be reported with no confirmatory alpha claims; p-values reported for completeness with adjusted interpretation. All reported exploratory analyses will be labeled as exploratory.
missingness_plan: API/model-call infrastructural failures: automatic retry policy up to 2 additional attempts spaced 30s apart for transient provider errors; if retries fail, mark that pipeline call as 'infrastructure failure' and apply primary analysis treatment (complete_pair_primary). If an LLM call returns malformed output that the transformation parser deterministically rejects, treat as 'parser-failure' and record as pipeline failure for that attempt; pipeline then proceeds to next allowed attempt until max attempts exhausted. No human adjudication is permitted; all rejections are deterministic (parsing exceptions, verifier input validation). Document counts of excluded pairs and include sensitivity analysis treating failures as zeros. Random seeds/Sampling reproducibility: task selection and per-attempt seeds are deterministic per the preregistered seeds list.

benchmark_names: Public NetOps task pool (NetConfEval-like public items)
risk_factors: Prompt leakage across tasks (model memory, cached contexts)
Training-set overlap / memorized templates in hosted model
Cross-contamination via reused prompt artifacts or identical task descriptions
detection_procedures: Record and hash all prompts and full model outputs per call; flag identical outputs across distinct tasks via deterministic content-hash comparison.
Detect high-output similarity using string-similarity (normalized Levenshtein) thresholds; flag items above 0.95 similarity for exclusion or sensitivity analysis.
Compare generated configs to task templates; if exact matches to a training-like example (deterministic string match to known public examples), mark as possible memorization and report separately.
item_flagging_rules: If output hash equals a known public-config hash from provenance list => flag and analyze separately (not excluded from primary analysis but reported).
If parser normalization fails deterministically => automatic rejection of that attempt; pipeline proceeds per retry policy.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis includes all unflagged pairs. Flagged memorized matches and high-similarity duplicates will be reported in a contamination table and excluded from a sensitivity re-analysis if their count exceeds 5% of the confirmatory sample.
residual_uncertainty: Possible undiscovered memorization not detected by deterministic matching; documented and reported.

budget_scenarios.description: Confirmatory-only execution using primary model (OpenAI/gpt-4o-mini) on N=132 paired tasks (stratified). LLM-only and GVR pipelines each have matched per-task max model-call budget = 4 (initial generate + up to 3 repair/alternative attempts).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Model-call accounting: per paired task, LLM-only may use up to 4 generation attempts and GVR up to 4 attempts; both pipelines executed per task => 4+4=8 calls per paired task. 132 paired tasks * 8 calls = 1056 total model calls. This is within the capability manifest model-call budget (maximum_planned_model_calls=10000) and comfortably feasible within the declared wall-clock constraints; verifier runs are CPU-only within containerized Batfish harness.

budget_scenarios.description: Expansive run: confirmatory set (N=132) on primary model + exploratory replication on second hosted model (Anthropic/claude-2.1) on additional exploratory N=40 tasks (same per-task budgets).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Model-call accounting: primary confirmatory model: 132 tasks * 8 calls = 1056 calls. Exploratory replication: 40 tasks * 8 calls = 320 calls. Total = 1056+320 = 1376 model calls. Still within the manifest limit of 10000 model calls and CPU-executable verifier harness.

power_plan.clustering_unit: task (paired episode: same task, two pipelines, same confirmatory model)
power_plan.calculation_method: Two-sided paired-proportions sample-size approximation (McNemar-style power approximation). Using alpha=0.05, power=0.80, target absolute paired difference=0.15, conservative baseline pass rate p0=0.30 (assumed) yields required paired N ≈ 132. Calculation details archived in power_calc.txt (artifact).
assumptions: Baseline (LLM-only) pass rate p0 assumed 0.30 based on prior-domain evidence and conservative estimate; alternative baseline used in sensitivity scenarios.
Pairwise dependence assumed moderate; calculation used conservative variance approximations.
Alpha two-sided = 0.05; power target = 0.80; bootstrap CI will be used to check robustness.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=132 and baseline p0=0.30, detectable absolute paired difference ≈ 0.15 at 80% power. If baseline is higher, detectable effect increases; sensitivity analyses will report detectable effect curves.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power post-hoc for observed baseline pass rate and report post-hoc minimum detectable effect.
If observed missingness / excluded pairs >10%, recompute and report reduced effective N and corresponding detectable effect.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip check: canonicalized config -> verifier input -> parsed back to canonical form; require exact string match (deterministic).
Property-preservation tests: for a held-out set of 20 reference configs, verify that canonicalization does not change reachability outcomes under the verifier.
automatic_rejection_rules: If parser raises deterministic exception or canonicalizer changes semantic tokens (detected by property-preservation test), mark attempt as 'parse-reject' and proceed per retry policy.
Reject outputs that fail schema validation (device names, interface format) deterministically; no human adjudication.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated audit: deterministically select 10% of successful passes per stratum using fixed RNG seed and re-run verifier end-to-end to confirm deterministic pass; any inconsistency triggers full re-execution of affected tasks.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: All mapping (e.g., natural-language entity -> device/interface mapping) implemented as deterministic rule-based functions with unit tests; mapping tables and unit-test results archived.
residual_risks: Edge-case parser bugs causing silent semantic changes (mitigated by round-trip and property-preservation tests but residual risk remains).

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Verifier expressivity coverage: the chosen Batfish harness covers reachability, ACL semantics, and basic routing-invariant checks, but cannot model vendor-specific hardware quirks or every operational semantic; claims will be explicitly bounded to verifier-covered properties.

Representativeness of the curated 132-task set for all operational NetOps workloads; we mitigate by publishing selection protocol and synthetic generator and labeling complexity, but external generalization beyond the sampled task bank remains untested.

Hosted LLM API nondeterminism and unseen model updates: although generation settings are deterministic (temperature=0) and outputs are archived, hosted model behavior can change over time; replication will be time-stamped and artifacts archived for audit.
